products.title: HALLOWED | Copper Golf Ball Marker
products.body_html:
🐙 HOLLOWED - The Den · 100 Units · Halloween 2026

Every October, millions of pumpkins get gutted, carved, lit for one night, and left on a porch to rot. Nothing about that ritual is built to last.

This one is.

Hollowed starts as solid copper, milled into a heavy coin with a scalloped edge you'll thumb on every walk to the green. Across the face runs a mummy wrap in stainless steel, cut and inlaid into the copper. Beneath the linen a jack-o-lantern grins out in bare copper, its eyes and mouth blackened deep. A single bat cuts across the rim.

About the name.

Before you carve a pumpkin, you hollow it. Before the Egyptians wrapped their dead, they did the same: everything taken out, the body bound in linen so it would outlast the world that buried it. The two rituals are thousands of years apart and share one idea. Empty it. Wrap it. Keep it forever.

It's also one letter off Hallowed.

The pumpkins on your street will be compost by Thanksgiving. This golf ball marker will darken in your pocket and stay bright where your thumb lands. In twenty years it will look like something excavated, not purchased.

36 grams. Set it behind your ball and it stays where you put it.

One hundred exist, because a hundred is what one man could mill, inlay and finish before the drop. When they're gone, Hollowed is retired for good and moves to the Vault with every design we've buried.

Most golfers mark their ball with whatever golf ball marker came free in the sleeve. Theirs gets thrown out with the decorations.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid milled copper body, natural finish that darkens with carry
  • Stainless steel mummy wrap inlay, hand-fitted
  • Bare copper jack-o-lantern face with blackened recesses
  • Engraved bat silhouette on the rim
  • Scalloped knurled edge for grip
  • Concentric machined reverse with engraved Kraken mark
  • 1.35" diameter × 0.1875" thick · 36g
  • Heavyweight golf ball marker and everyday carry coin
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade (certificate of authenticity)
  • Limited to 100 units. Design permanently retired after this drop.

Empty it. Wrap it. Keep it forever.

products.title: Blacklist 042: GRAY MATTER
products.body_html:
GRAY MATTER - Blacklist No. 042 

Every course has a guy you don't want to draw in a match. It isn't the long hitter. It's the quiet one. He's already read the green, already worked out the wind, already decided how your afternoon ends. You don't see it coming because it doesn't look like anything. It looks like a man thinking.

Gray Matter is that man with the mask on.

The body is black anodized aluminum, milled EDC style, with a scalloped edge cut for the thumb. On the left is a mane of wild hair cut from stainless steel and inlaid by hand, every lock unfolding off the face like it never once met a comb. On the right is the mask, a separate stainless inlay drilled for breath and marked in red paint engravings. Two pieces of steel sit fitted side by side. Half of it is the greatest mind in the room. The other half is the reason the room went quiet.

Look through the eyehole. Something looks back.

Turn it over. The Blacklist mark runs edge to edge across the reverse, oversized and cut over the Kraken engraved dead center. This marks the few. It means what it says.

15 grams. It's a golf ball marker that rides in the pocket without announcing itself. Neither does he.

Fourty exist, because fourty is how many faces one man could inlay, fit, and box before the drop. When the last one goes, the file moves to the Vault with every design we've retired, and Gray Matter never runs again.

Most golfers mark their ball with whatever golf ball marker fell out of the sleeve. Blacklist marks it with something that's already thinking three holes ahead.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Black anodized aluminum body, CNC milled 
  • Scalloped EDC-style edge for grip
  • Stainless steel hair inlay, hand-fitted
  • Separate stainless steel mask inlay with red paint-filled engravings
  • Oversize Blacklist mark on reverse, engraved over a center Kraken mark
  • 1.35" diameter × 0.1875" thick · 15g
  • Golf ball marker and everyday carry coin
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade (certificate of authenticity)
  • Blacklist only. Limited to 40 units. Design permanently retired after this drop.

Brains on the outside. Steel where the conscience goes.

products.title: 🐙 THEORY - Golf Pitch Tool
products.body_html:
🐙 THEORY - Pitch Tool

Par is someone else's idea of how a hole should be played.

THEORY is for the golfer who never accepted that. Solid brass, machined and finished by hand, built around one belief: the best shot on the card is usually the one nobody else saw.

The front carries a portrait of the most famous wild-haired mind of the last century, engraved deep into the brass. He did his best work in his head long before anyone took it seriously. The reverse states the position plainly: IMAGINATION > PAR, signed with the Kraken mark.

The brass is darkened to an aged bronze, and it won't stay that way. Every repaired pitch mark, every pocket, every round wears the high points back to bright gold. In a few seasons it will look like it belonged to someone before you, and in a few decades it will.

At 32 grams and a quarter inch thick, this pitch tool has real weight in the hand. The tines are tapered to go into the green clean and lift without tearing, and the ring sits on a finger between shots.

THEORY is a permanent piece, for now. Each one is still made to order by the same pair of hands in the same shop, so there's a short wait. Good theories take time.

The golfer with a plastic divot tool from the pro shop bin is playing the hole as drawn. This one plays it as imagined.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid brass body, hand finished
  • Aged brass patina that wears to bright brass with use
  • Deep laser-engraved portrait, front
  • IMAGINATION > PAR with Kraken mark, reverse
  • Tapered tines for clean pitch mark repair
  • Ring head for a secure grip and finger carry
  • 2.8" long × 1.12" wide × 0.25" thick · 32g
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade, certificate of authenticity
  • Made to order in Acushnet, MA. Lead time applies.
  • No-questions-asked returns and exchanges

Every round starts as a theory.

products.body_html:

Every castle had one room no army ever reached.

The Keep. The last wall. The place the crown went when everything else fell.

This golf ball marker was built in that spirit. A keyhole of solid copper, its border cut stone by stone like the walls of a fortress. Inside, a stainless steel skull: the watchman who never leaves his post. Beside him, Dollaro red leather, deep as a chamber the world was never meant to see.

Turn it over and the key is waiting, engraved with three words: Kept, Not Given.

That's the point. Most things you buy. This golf ball marker is one you keep, on the green, in your pocket, and eventually in someone else's hands when you pass it down. The copper darkens with every round and records where you've been. No two will age alike.

Every piece is milled, inlaid and finished by hand in a one-man shop, and that's the only reason the run is this small. When it's gone, The Keep is retired to the Vault for good. No restock. No second edition. Just the few who got through the gate.

Mark your ball with a golf ball marker worth guarding.

products.body_html:
🐇 BLACKLIST 041: HARE'S BREADTH 

Some putts die on the lip. Yours drop on the last quarter turn.

Call it luck. You know better. Luck is fickle, and it only shows up for the golfer who keeps walking into the blades anyway.

Hare's Breadth is the golf ball marker for that golfer. A stainless steel rabbit, mid-leap, inlaid into solid copper. Around it, a storm of swords and running hares engraved across the face. Above the chaos, one line: May Luck Find You.

He clears every blade. By a hair.

Set this golf ball marker down and the green goes quiet. Your foursome will ask to hold it. They'll feel 35 grams of copper and steel, run a thumb along the scalloped EDC edge, and understand it has nothing in common with the stamped, merch-tent golf ball marker in their own pocket.

Every golf ball marker in this run is milled, inlaid, and finished by one man in a one-man shop. That is why only 30 exist. Once they're claimed, the design is locked in the Vault, never to be made again.

products.title: MACHIYA - The House Mark · Stainless Steel
products.body_html:
MACHIYA - The House Mark · Stainless Steel · Permanent Stock

The roof came off the coin that was never released.

No logo. No name. No number. Just a house, milled from solid stainless steel, sitting behind your ball while the rest of the group tries to work out what it is. The ones who know won't ask.

Why a house.

It's a machiya - the merchant townhouse of old Kyoto. Narrow at the street, deep behind it. The front room was the shop. The back was where the family lived. One roof over the work and the life, because the man who made the thing was the man who sold it and the man who slept above it.

Kyoto tore most of them down. Concrete went up faster and cheaper and nobody argued. The machiya still standing are standing because somebody refused - paid more to keep something old than it would have cost to replace it with something new.

That's the house Kraken is built in. The mill runs twenty feet from the kitchen. Every piece is cut, finished and boxed by the same pair of hands. So the house became the mark, and this golf ball marker is the mark with nothing else on it.

It's milled as an open frame. Window cut clean through, gable cut clean through, so the green shows through it when you set it down. The tool paths are left on the face exactly as the mill drew them. Ten grams. It disappears in a pocket until you need it.

Nearly everything made here runs once and goes to the Vault. The house doesn't. It stays (at least for now), milled in small batches between drops by the same man who makes everything else. When a batch is gone, it's gone until he gets back to the mill.

A factory golf ball marker says you took what was handed to you. This one says which house you belong to.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid stainless steel, CNC milled 
  • Machiya rooftop silhouette - the Kraken House Mark
  • Open-frame construction, window and gable cut through
  • Natural machined finish, tool paths left visible
  • No logo, no engraving. The roof is the mark.
  • 1.3" wide at widest point × 0.1875" thick · 10g
  • Low-profile golf ball marker and everyday carry piece
  • Ships with its Promenade - certificate of authenticity
  • Milled in small batches.

One roof. One pair of hands.

products.title: CUT LINE | Black Oxide Carbon Steel
products.body_html:
🐙 CUT LINE | Black Oxide Carbon Steel | The Den

Every tournament has a number. Shoot it, and you play the weekend. Miss it by one, and you're packing the car Friday afternoon while someone else takes your tee time.

You don't repair a pitch mark with this. You make the cut. It comes out of your pocket black as a closed course at midnight, and the green goes quiet for a breath. There's no polish and no shine, just carbon steel that looks like it means business.

The scissor form is the lie. Slim, elegant, almost delicate between two fingers. Then you turn it over and find KRAKEN cut down the full length of the blade in Oswald capitals, laser-marked through the black oxide to the bare steel underneath. A single small Kraken mark sits on the front at the pivot. The form is refined. The finish is not. That tension is the whole point.

Machined from solid carbon steel and finished in black oxide. The marks aren't printed or painted. The laser burns away the finish to reveal the raw metal, so the brand is literally what's underneath. And it doesn't stop there. Carbon steel is a living metal. Over time the oxide will wear at the edges and contact points where your fingers find it, and the steel will start showing through. Every round leaves its mark. Five years from now, nobody else's will look like yours.

You don't buy a golf pitch tool. You buy proof you made the cut.

CUT LINE is part of The Den. Once it sells out, the design is retired permanently to the Vault. There won't be another.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Material: Solid carbon steel, CNC machined
  • Length: 3.00"
  • Width at widest: 1.67"
  • Thickness at spine: 3/16"
  • Weight: 23g
  • Finish: Black oxide
  • Front: Kraken mark, laser-marked to bare steel
  • Back: Oswald "KRAKEN" wordmark down the blade, laser-marked to bare steel
  • Edition: Den drop, retired forever once sold out
  • Promenade: Numbered certificate of authenticity included

🛠 CARING FOR CARBON STEEL

Carbon steel isn't stainless. It's the same steel used in heirloom knives and classic tools, and it rewards a little attention.

  • It ships oiled. That thin film is what protects the steel. Leave it on.
  • Wipe it dry after the round, especially after wet grass, rain, or morning dew.
  • Re-oil every few weeks, or after it gets wet. A drop of mineral oil, gun oil, or 3-in-1 rubbed on with a soft cloth does the job.
  • Store it dry. A pocket or a pouch is fine. A damp bag pocket for a month is not.
  • If you see surface rust, rub it out with a few drops of oil on a soft cloth, then wipe and re-oil.
  • Expect wear. Bright steel showing through the black oxide at the edges is patina, not damage. It's the tool becoming yours.

Some guys go home Friday.

Limited drop. Once it's gone, it's gone.

products.title: Blacklist 040: FACE VALUE
products.body_html:
FACE VALUE - Blacklist No. 40

In 1862 the country ran out of coins. People paid in stamps.

That's what a stamp is. Money you can mail. A number in the corner and Washington in the oval, same as the dollar. Good for exactly what it says.

Until somebody wants it. Then the number in the corner stops mattering.

Face Value is the five-cent blue, laser annealed on milled titanium. Nothing redrawn. The portrait, the laurels, U.S. POSTAGE across the top, the fives in the corners, the perforated edge milled one tooth at a time. Blue, because blue meant the letter was leaving the country.

Then the lines. Laser annealed across the finished face, through the blue, down to bare titanium. A cancellation means it's been spent. It's the last operation on every piece. Forty pieces. Fourty cancellations. 

Turn it over. The Kraken. ACUSHNET MASS. The date it left.

You've seen the coin. You've seen the note. You've seen the card. This is the one that was already spent.

The file moves to the Vault with every design we've retired.

Most golfers mark with whatever golf ball marker came free in the mail. Blacklist carries the one worth more than the number in the corner.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid milled titanium body
  • Blue anodized face, laser annealed back to bare titanium
  • Original five-cent blue design: portrait oval, laurels, corner numerals
  • Perforated edge, milled tooth by tooth
  • Cancellation lines laser annealed in black
  • Reverse: Kraken mark, Acushnet postmark and drop date
  • 1.3" tall x 1" wide weighing 20g
  • A titanium golf ball marker built to outlast the bag
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade - certificate of authenticity
  • Blacklist only. Limited to 40 units. Design permanently retired after this drop.

Spent once. Cancelled for good.

products.title: 🟡 NASSAU | Brass + Dollaro Leather
products.body_html:
🟡 NASSAU | Brass + Dollaro Leather | Permanent Collection

Some men play for fun. Others play for something.

The ones worth playing with always have a little riding on it: front nine, back nine, overall. Two-dollar Nassau or two hundred, it was never about the money. It's about the drive home knowing you took it.

Nassau is for those men.

Milled from solid brass and shaped like the bag the winnings go home in, this marker carries weight in every sense. On its face, dark green Dollaro leather is inlaid into the brass. It's a grain named for the texture of a dollar bill, so it's money leather on a money bag. A raised brass dollar sign sits in the center, just in case anyone missed the point.

On the back, there's brushed brass and a single engraved Kraken mark. That's all the signature it needs.

This isn't a ball marker. It's what you put down when there's money on the line.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Material: Solid brass, CNC machined
  • Inlay: Genuine Dollaro leather in dark green
  • Face: Raised brass dollar sign
  • Back Engraving: Kraken mark, laser-engraved
  • Weight: 20g
  • Height: 1.34"
  • Width: 1"" at widest point
  • Thickness: 0.1875"
  • Finish: Brushed brass
  • Includes: Promenade, a certificate of authenticity

products.title: THIRD LIFE · King Cold, Life III of IX
products.body_html:
Nine lives. This is the third.

King Cold came back again, and this time he came back in steel. Brass was the second life, warm and polished. Something changed on the way through. Life three is harder, heavier, and colder to the touch. You held the marker, then the scissor blade. Now he's armored.

Look at the face. The crown is still there, and so is the head, cut in brass and set into the steel. But one eye is an X. That's a life he's already spent, and he wears it where everybody can see it. The other eye is still open and watching you line up your putt. He knows exactly how many lives he has left. 

Behind him, the resin is ice: blue and aqua, layered with texture, frozen in place. Turn it over and the back is fully putter milled steel with a graffiti K floating in the same frozen blue. It's the street tag on the back of a crown.

Solid stainless steel, 38 grams, a quarter inch thick. It hits the green with weight and sits in the pocket like it was issued, not bought. The front carries the fine linear tool paths straight off the mill. The back is putter machined for grip. The brass will warm with every round, and the steel won't care.

This isn't a golf pitch tool you grab from the pro shop bucket. It's the third life of a character your foursome already knows.

THIRD LIFE is Life III of IX in the King Cold series, part of The Den. Once it sells out, the design is retired permanently to the Vault. King Cold will return, but never as this. There won't be another.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Material: Solid stainless steel, CNC machined
  • Length: 2.85"
  • Width: 0.85"
  • Thickness: 0.25"
  • Weight: 38g
  • Front: Brass King Cold inlay (crown, X eye, glass eye) over textured blue and aqua resin
  • Reverse: Knurled stainless with a graffiti K set in blue and aqua resin
  • Finish: Linear machined face, putter face-milled back
  • Series: King Cold, Nine Lives, Life III of IX
  • Promenade: Numbered certificate of authenticity included

Two lives down. He remembers both.

products.title: NACRE Golf Ball Marker
products.body_html:
An abalone builds its shell the slow way. It lays down a microscopic sheet of nacre, then another on top of it, for years in cold water, until the layers catch light the way nothing man-made can. No two shells grow the same, and no two patterns repeat.

Nacre is built around that. It's a milled, solid stainless steel body with real abalone shell inlaid across the face and the Kraken mark standing up out of it in raised steel. Turn it in the light and the shell moves from green to violet to blue and back. The back is brushed steel with a small Kraken mark centered, quiet and clean.

products.title: HARDHAT BALL MARKER
products.body_html:
Every course has a place where the water starts and the courage stops.

The men who wore this helmet didn't have that place. Fifty-six pounds of brass and copper bolted over their heads, one hose to the surface, and the bottom of a harbor nobody could see into. They did the work by feel. Alone. Cold. Finished before anyone up top knew what it cost. They didn't call themselves divers. They called themselves hardhats.

Hardhat is built in the same three metals the real helmets were. The body is solid milled copper with a scalloped EDC edge that finds your thumb on the walk up. Set into it, a stainless steel field laser-annealed to a deep ocean blue - the color isn't paint or plating, it's the steel itself, heated until it turns - with the waves cut into it. And riding the swell, a brass Mark V diving helmet, engraved and darkened into every recess, so the bolts and ports read from across the green.

Turn it over. Kraken mark, centered. Nothing else. The thing that lives below the waterline doesn't need to announce itself.

That's the whole idea. The kraken is down there. Everyone knows it. Everyone lays up. Hardhat is the golf ball marker for the one who goes in anyway - the one who aims at the pin over the water on 17 because the water was never the point.

Copper darkens. The edge polishes where your thumb rides. In five years this golf ball marker will look like it came off a wreck, because it went everywhere you did.

When the last one goes the file is retired and Hardhat never runs again - it moves to the Vault with every design we've buried.

Everyone else stays on the boat.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid milled copper body, scalloped EDC edge
  • 303 stainless steel inlay, laser-annealed ocean blue with engraved wave pattern
  • Brass Mark V diving helmet inlay, laser-engraved with darkened recesses
  • Laser-engraved Kraken mark, reverse, centered
  • 1.35" diameter × 0.1875" thick · 35g
  • Heavyweight golf ball marker and everyday carry coin
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade - certificate of authenticity
  • Limited to 100 units. Design permanently retired after this drop.

Below the waterline. Carry it accordingly.

products.title: BENCH SKETCH HOODIE
products.body_html:
Every Kraken piece starts the same way. Not in software. On the bench, with a pen, on whatever's nearest - the back of a Promenade proof, a yardage book, the shop notebook with copper shavings in the spine. Most of those drawings get milled into steel and the paper goes in the bin.

This one didn't get cleaned up. It got printed exactly as it was drawn.

The back is the sketch: a Kraken in one take, hand-lettered KRAK above it, banded tentacles, the linework a little crooked where the pen moved faster than the plan. No vector pass, no smoothing, no second draft. It's the drawing that would normally be the first step toward a golf ball marker, left as the finished thing instead.

The front is quiet. The Kraken mark, stitched in gold thread at the left chest, small enough that only the people who know, know. Woven KRAKEN tag at the right hem. That's the whole front.

Midweight fleece in navy, classic fit, built for the drive to the course in October and the bar after. Soft enough to live in, heavy enough to hold its shape when it's been washed a hundred times.

Most golf hoodies were designed by a committee. This one was drawn by the guy who runs the mill.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Midweight cotton-blend fleece, navy, classic fit
  • Full-back screenprint: original hand-drawn Kraken and KRAK lettering, gold ink, printed from the raw sketch
  • Kraken mark embroidered in gold thread, left chest
  • Woven KRAKEN tag, right hem
  • Jersey-lined hood, front pouch pocket, ribbed cuffs and hem
  • Unisex sizing, S-3XL

products.title: Oculus Ball Marker
products.body_html:
Oculus is the window set high in a cathedral facade - the one built so a single beam of light lands in the same spot every day at the same hour. Not a window you look out of. A window that looks back.

That's the shape of this piece. A gothic arch laser-engraved into solid brass - not stamped, not cast, machined and worked by hand the way cathedral fittings were before anyone thought to make it faster. Through the arch: a rosette with a single open eye at its center, a tentacle rising out of engraved waves toward it. Every line you see is cut into the metal. No plating. No paint. Nothing that sits on top of the brass instead of in it.

Flip it over and there's just the Kraken. Nothing else. That side is for you.

Set this golf ball marker down on the 18th green and it stops looking like a golf accessory and starts looking like something pulled off a cathedral door that only opens for members. Someone's going to ask about it. You're going to tell them you can't get one.

Because you can't. I make a run, I move on to the next thing, and the people who were paying attention own the only ones that will ever exist.

If you own this, you're the kind of golfer who notices the window before you notice what's through it.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Machined Solid brass, laser-engraved
  • Gothic stained glass window silhouette - 1.4" tall × 0.88" wide × 0.1875" thick
  • 28 grams - enough weight to sit flat in wind, light enough to forget it's in your pocket
  • Front: Kraken eye and tentacle stained glass scene, hand-engraved
  • Back: Kraken logo, brushed brass
  • Will darken and patina naturally with wear - part of the piece, not a flaw in it
  • Ships with its Promenade certificate of authenticity

The light only hits this window once a day. Claim your golf ball marker before it's a story you tell.

products.title: HEARTLESS V2 - Black Stainless Steel
products.body_html:
🐙 HEARTLESS II 

Every golfer you've ever feared on the back nine had one thing in common. Nothing got to them. Not the water left, not the three-footer for the match, not the guy in the group talking through their backswing. That's not coldness. That's what it looks like when the thing driving you sits somewhere nobody else can reach.

Heartless II is a rib cage. Solid stainless steel, CNC-milled, with the rib cage tack welded to the body. The finish is exactly what came off the machine - the concentric tool paths, the weld color at the edges, nothing polished away to hide how it was made. It looks raw because it is.

Look through the ribs. Where the heart should be, there's a Kraken - this time cut from blackened stainless steel, not gold. No shine, no giveaway. It sits loose inside the cavity the same way its predecessor did. Tilt the marker and it slides. Set it down and it settles. Drop it on the bar and you'll hear it before anyone sees it - and this time, even if they look, there's nothing catching the light to find.

That's the idea. Steel on the outside, steel where the heart should be, and the only proof it's there at all is the sound it makes when it moves.

At 37 grams and poker chip size, it lands on the green with some authority. Thumb the ribs on the walk up. Mark your ball with it. Pick it up and feel the Kraken shift back into place.

Most golfers carry whatever golf ball marker fell out of a sleeve. This one carries a heart nobody can see and everybody can hear.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Solid stainless steel body, CNC milled
  • Laser cut, tack welded stainless steel ribs
  • Blackened stainless steel Kraken, free-floating inside the chest cavity
  • Natural machined finish - mill marks and weld color left as-is, smooth to the touch
  • 1.53" tall × 1.47" wide × 0.26" thick · 37g
  • Poker chip footprint, heavyweight golf ball marker and everyday carry
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade - certificate of authenticity
  • Design permanently retired after this drop.

Steel outside. Steel within. Some hearts don't shine - they just don't stop.

products.title: HOBO LUCK GOLF BALL MARKER - TIMASCUS EDITION
products.body_html:
🔮 HOBO LUCK BALL MARKER - TIMASCUS EDITION


A Kraken classic - reborn in metal that didn't exist when the game was invented.

This is the Hobo Luck Ball Marker in Timascus, and it doesn't fake its scars. It earns its color. Timascus is layered titanium alloys forge-welded into a single billet, then heat-colored in the shop - no paint, no plating, no coating. The purple, blue, and gold you see is oxide on titanium, coaxed out by flame and timing. Get it wrong by a few seconds and the whole piece goes back to bare metal. Every one of these came off the torch a little different because there is no way to make them the same.

The front carries the Hobo Luck engraving in full - horseshoe, clover, the hand of cards, LIBERTY and LUCK stamped in like a rail-yard tattoo, 777 and 1937 tucked in for anyone who reads the details. Old-world craft, outsider grit, and the belief that luck isn't found. It's forged. The back is stripped down to the Kraken cut clean through the center, so the layers show all the way to the core.

Scalloped EDC edges are milled, not stamped. The banding runs through the thickness, not across the surface, so the pattern on the rim is the same pattern inside the metal. Drop it, pocket it, scrape it against a hundred coins - it doesn't wear off because it isn't on. It's in.

This isn't a finish. This is what the material is.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES:

  • Material: Timascus - forge-welded layered titanium alloys, lighter than brass, harder than the game deserves
  • Finish: Heat-anodized in-house; no dyes, no coatings, no two the same
  • Engraving: Full Hobo Luck front detail; Kraken cutout back
  • Edges: Machined scallops for grip and a profile you'll recognize in the dark
  • Dimensions: 1.35" diameter × ~0.19" thick
  • Weight: 18g of titanium that will outlast the bag it rides in
  • Comes with the Promenade certificate of authenticity 

⚠️ Note: Titanium oxide color shifts subtly with angle and light. The piece in your hand will not photograph exactly like the piece in these photos, and neither will anyone else's. That's the whole point of a golf ball marker made in a one-man shop instead of a factory. Windex wipe to bring back the brillance! 

💥 If you don't believe in luck, but you still carry it anyway - carry it in the one metal that couldn't be faked if someone tried.

products.title: Blacklist 038 - Murex Fred Toolholder
products.body_html:
🐙 MUREX - Fred Tool Holder · Blacklist No. 038 · 30 Units

Luxury in Contrast. Built for the Few.

The Fred Tool Holder - Murex Edition is the first leather toolholder piece Kraken has ever made for Blacklist, and it doesn't arrive quietly. White on the outside. Purple underneath. Named for the sea snail that gave the ancient world its only true purple.

The murex is an unremarkable-looking thing - a chalk-white ridged shell you'd step over on the beach. Split it open and there's a single gland that bleeds a dye no one could replicate for three thousand years. It took twelve thousand snails to produce a gram and a half of it. Rome made it law: purple was the emperor's color, and wearing it without the rank was a capital offense. You didn't buy your way into it. You were granted it.

That's the whole piece in one object. Conceria Walpier Hatch Buttero veg-tan in white, textured so fine it reads like linen in the hand. Fold it open and purple croc-stamped veg-tan runs the spine - scaled, deep, and completely hidden until you're the one holding it. Everyone at the green sees the white. Only you see the purple.

Every stitch is hand-sewn - black French saddle stitch, pulled by hand, two needles, one pass at a time, the way it's been done since before anyone thought to speed it up. Edges hand-burnished to a satin close. The Kraken mark is foil-stamped in black on the back, quiet against the white.

Here's the part the murex earns: Tyrian purple didn't fade in sunlight. It deepened. Everything else the ancient world dyed washed out and went gray - the murex went richer with age and exposure. Veg-tan does exactly the same thing. Six months in your bag, the white will warm to bone and honey, the purple will drink down darker, and the piece will look like something you inherited rather than something you ordered.

Slide open the snap closure and load up your tools:

  • Front pocket: fits your favorite Kraken golf ball marker
  • Rear pocket: stores your divot tool, tees, or that post-round bill you've earned

Thirty exist, because thirty is what one man could cut, stitch, burnish and stamp. When they're gone the piece is retired and Murex never runs again - it moves to the Vault with everything else we've buried.

The golfer pulling a factory pouch out of his bag is telling you he didn't think about it. This one tells a different story, and it tells it in a color you used to be executed for wearing.

🧵 SPECS & FEATURES

  • Materials: Conceria Walpier Hatch Buttero Italian veg-tanned leather in white (linen-texture hatch grain) + purple croc-stamped veg-tanned leather
  • Thread: Black - hand saddle-stitched, French stitch
  • Design: Dual-tone construction, snap closure, front golf ball marker pocket + rear stash pocket
  • Finish: Hand-burnished edges, satin sheen
  • Mark: Black foil-stamped Kraken logo, reverse panel
  • Dimensions (closed): 3.75" × 2.5"
  • Edition: Blacklist exclusive - limited to 30 units, ships with its numbered Promenade
  • Built to carry a Kraken golf ball marker, divot tool, tees, and a folded bill
  • Design permanently retired after this drop

⚠️ Each Murex is unique - croc placement, hatch grain, and stitch spacing vary slightly. Veg-tan will darken and evolve with play, building a patina as personal as your game.

White outside. Purple inside. Same as the shell it's named for.

products.title: HOLY WATER — Ball Marker
products.body_html:
Every hazard is holy.

A cathedral window rendered in metal - rose window at the crown, tentacles grown through the tracery where stone mullions should be, waves breaking at the sill. Then somebody tagged it.

That's the whole idea. Sacred architecture and the hand that defaces it, sitting in the same 1.4 inches. Reverence and irreverence, milled into one piece.

The body is cut from a solid block of 303 stainless steel - not cast, not stamped. You can read the tool path across the face, a fingerprint no two markers share. The inlay is laser-cut from brass stock, laser-engraved with the window, and seated into the pocket so the brass sits proud against the raw steel. Brass will patina with your hands and the weather. The steel won't. Over a season the two surfaces separate - warm against cold, aged against new. That's intended.

At 25 grams it has the weight of something that was made, not sourced. Heavy enough to stay put in wind. Small enough to disappear in a pocket.

Reverse face carries the Kraken mark. Arrives with its Promenade, hand-numbered.

This design is one-and-done. When the drop closes, HOLY WATER is retired permanently - never re-run, never restocked. What you own is what exists.

products.title: 🏴 The Manifesto Hoodie - Navy
products.body_html:
The pro shop sells you what everyone else is wearing.

That's the point. That's the business model. Generic logos on generic fits, marked up four times, stacked next to the cart girl's tip jar. The whole industry trained an entire generation of golfers to dress like a sponsorship deck.

You stopped pretending years ago.

The Manifesto Hoodie is what you put on when you're done playing along. Front-loaded with three words that filter your tribe - REJECT THE PRO SHOP - sprayed on like graffiti on a harbor wall. Arm patch marked with coordinates only the right people will recognize: + ACUSHNET 41° 41' N / 70° 54' W. A huge town in golf. The town we still make Kraken in. The town the pro shop forgot.

This isn't a hoodie. It's a position.

You wear it to the range and the regulars notice. You wear it to the clubhouse and the wrong people look away. You wear it on the back nine when the round's slipping and the wind's picking up and somehow you play better, because the hoodie reminds you what you came here for in the first place - and it wasn't the pro shop's blessing.

Wear what you stand for. Or stand for nothing.

🎯 SPECS & FEATURES

  • 8.5 oz midweight fleece - substantial without overheating
  • Ring-spun cotton face yarn, 32 singles - smooth hand, premium print surface
  • Jersey-lined hood for structure and comfort
  • Heavy-gauge drawcord with metal eyelets
  • Double-needle stitching throughout
  • Split-stitch seams for durability
  • Twill neck tape for clean finish
  • 1x1 rib cuffs and waistband
  • Standard retail fit - built for layering or wearing solo
  • Front: spray-painted "REJECT THE PRO SHOP / KRAKEN GOLF CO." with @KG  corner mark
  • Back: blank
  • Soft-hand DTF print, matte finish - wash-tested for long-term wear
  • Custom Kraken Golf Co. woven label on bottom hem
  • Made-to-order - your golf ball marker brand built one piece at a time

Sizing: Unisex XS through 3XL. Standard retail fit. Order true to size for a fitted silhouette, size up for a more relaxed wear.

Production: Made when you order it. Allow approximately one week for production, plus shipping. Tracking sent the moment it ships.

👑 NOT FOR EVERYONE

The Manifesto Hoodie is for the golfer who knows their handicap and refuses to be one. Who's been around long enough to see what the sport became - and old enough to remember what it used to be. Who'd rather wear a piece nobody else owns than a logo everyone does.

If the pro shop's still your benchmark, this isn't your hoodie.

products.title: LAST LAUGH
products.body_html:
LAST LAUGH
The Den · One-and-Done

Two faces, one marker. On the left, a grin. On the right, the grin that outlasts everyone - a skull, still smiling. Machined from a solid billet of aircraft-grade aluminum and finished in a pink anodize that has no business being this hard, Last Laugh is a memento mori for people who'd rather laugh at the back nine than fear it.

The face is split down the center: a brass smiley inlay on one half, a stainless steel skull on the other - two metals, hand-set, aging on their own terms. The EDC edge is cut with a gear-tooth grip that seats between your fingers and reads unmistakably from across the green. Flip it over and the Kraken is engraved into the back, because the people who know, know.

This is not a marker you lose. It's the one you set down slow, and pick up slower.

The Details

  • Pink anodized 6061 aluminum body
  • Brass smiley inlay / stainless steel skull inlay
  • Gear-tooth EDC edge
  • Kraken logo engraved on reverse
  • 1.35" diameter · 0.1875" thick · 18g
  • Ships with its numbered Promenade - certificate of authenticity, proof you were there

One design. One run. Retired forever once The Den sells out.
When it's gone, it's gone. Somebody's going to have the last laugh - make sure it's you.

products.title: Blacklist 036: Compound
products.body_html:
Machined Brass · Limited to 30

Einstein called compound interest the eighth wonder of the world. He who understands it, earns it; he who doesn't, pays it. Golf is the same equation - small edges, stacked over a lifetime, until the math tips in your favor. Compound is a monument to the players who understand that.

Machined from solid brass into a money bag, weighted to sit dead-flat on the green. The face carries the $ in raised relief, backed by four inlays - 23 in brushed stainless steel, 2 in hot-pink resin and set to drip behind the sign like the payoff spilling over. Flip it: Einstein stares back, Kraken-eyed, the genius behind the money. Two faces, one story. The mind on one side. What it earns on the other.

This is the smart money's mark. You don't explain it. The ones who get it, get it.

One design. Retired the moment it sells out. 

Specs

  • Solid machined brass, 20g - heavy in the hand, planted on the green
  • 1.25" at widest point · 0.1875" thick
  • 2 brushed "drip" stainless steel inlays + 2 hot-pink 3D-printed resin background inlays
  • Raised $ relief front · Einstein reverse with signature Kraken eyes
  • Includes numbered Promenade certificate of authenticity
  • Blacklist 036 - permanent retirement upon sellout

Everyone's got a rotation. This one lives in yours.

Solid brass, engraved on both faces with a light sole tread - the pattern that's been under more feet than any silhouette in sneaker history, now cut into metal built to outlast every pair it's ever walked with. The front carries the real weight: a stainless steel Kraken sneaker inlay, tentacle mark worked into the side panel where a logo would sit, set against a hand-fit resin graffiti inlay spelling KRAK in pink and blue - raw, tagged, unmistakably street.

This isn't a golf accessory wearing streetwear as a costume. It's a Kraken piece that happens to carry a driver. Carry it in the bag, carry it in the pocket, carry it anywhere your rotation goes.

One-and-done. Once The Den sells through, this design doesn't come back.

There's a reason men have worn signet rings for centuries. Not for decoration - for identity. A mark pressed into wax, a signature nobody could forge, a symbol that said this belongs to me before a name ever needed to be spoken.

The Signet carries that same weight into your pocket.

Slide it onto your finger and the ring settles like it was built for exactly that purpose - because it was. Solid 303 stainless steel, cold and substantial in the hand, with KRAKEN cut straight and clean beneath the band. Flip it over and our mark sits quiet on the reverse - no noise, no oversell, just the emblem doing what a seal has always done.

This isn't a tool you lose in a bag pocket. It's a tool you wear.

products.title: Blacklist 035: Amaterasu
products.body_html:
BLACKLIST 035: AMATERASU
Timascus Ball Marker - Limited to 30

Named for the sun goddess of Japanese myth - the deity from whom emperors traced their line - Amaterasu is a sunrise over Mt. Fuji rendered in metal, and retired the moment the last of thirty finds its owner.

The sacred mountain is hand-inlaid in a mix of charred stainless below and mirror-polished stainless steel for its snowcap breaking into drifting clouds set into the same. Behind it, a brass sky carries a whisper of the seigaiha wave - the ancient pattern of the sea that gives Kraken its name. And cresting the summit, the sun itself: a raised dome of burnt orange, the one warm breath of color against the cool metal.

All of it rides on a solid timascus round, no two alike - the alloy's grain flowing in ribbons of violet, gold, and blue that shift with every turn under the light. Flip it and you'll find a single word in Japanese script: KRAKEN.

This is not a marker you lose in a pocket. It's the piece you set down on the green and watch someone lean in to look at.

Thirty exist. When they're gone, the design is sealed forever. Each arrives with its numbered Promenade - your certificate that this one was yours.

products.title: BEDROCK - Copper Golf Ball Marker
products.body_html:
🪨 BEDROCK - Copper Golf Ball Marker | Core Collection

Everything else disappears. This doesn't.

Every Kraken design retires to The Vault the moment it sells out - gone, never made again. BEDROCK is the exception. It's the layer underneath a brand built on things you can't get twice. The one piece that's still there when the drop you missed is somebody else's story.

Machined from solid copper billet, then glass bead blasted to a warm matte satin that doesn't shine so much as smolder - then blackened for the antique look. The Kraken rises from the center in raised copper linework - clean, deliberate, cut across a field of fractured stone.

That field is a stone-formed composite core, built layer on layer, the same way the real thing gets made. Pressure. Time. Sediment. Set flush into the copper and locked.

Flip it and the back is left raw. Mill texture still on the surface, a small Kraken struck into the face. No polish, no cover-up. Proof that a person stood at a bench and made this, not a machine that never stopped running.

This golf ball marker is for the golfer who doesn't need to win a countdown to prove anything. Who walked past the pro shop wall and kept walking. Who carries one thing that's real instead of five that aren't.

Set it down on the green and it sits there like it belongs to the ground it's marking.

SPECS & FEATURES

  • Material: Solid copper with stone-formed composite inlay
  • Metal Finish: Glass bead blast, matte satin with darkening treatment
  • Dimensions: 1.25 in diameter × 0.1875 in thick
  • Weight: 22g
  • Detail: Raised Kraken linework, raw-finished reverse with struck Kraken mark
  • Availability: Core Collection - permanent stock, not a Vault retirement
  • Includes the Promenade, your certificate of authenticity

Some pieces vanish. This one holds.

products.title: SECOND LIFE - King Cold, Life II/IX
products.body_html:
Nine lives. This is the second.

King Cold doesn't retire. He dies and comes back - colder, sharper, wearing a new form every time the Vault closes behind the last one. You held the marker. Now you hold the blade. The set was never finished until this.

You don't fix a pitch mark with this. You settle it. The brass catches the light as it leaves your pocket and the green goes quiet for a breath - a crowned head, bared and watching, and a single word milled into the shaft like a verdict: COLD. This isn't a cat you pet. It's a cat that surveys the whole course and decides who's worth its time.

The scissor form is the lie. Slim, elegant, almost civil between two fingers. Then you see the crown. The head. The mark that says this thing has been here before and will be here again - nine times over. The form is refined. The character is feral. That tension is the whole point.

Machined from a single block of solid brass billet. Brushed, engraved, and weighted to sit in the hand like an heirloom - because that's what it is. The recesses will darken. The brushed surfaces will warm. Five years from now this piece will look like it has always belonged to you.

You don't buy a golf pitch tool. You buy the second life of a character your friends recognize before you say a word.

SECOND LIFE is Life II of IX in the King Cold series, part of The Den. Once it sells out, the design is retired permanently to the Vault. King Cold will return - but never as this. There will not be another.

  • Wordmark: "COLD" milled at the pivot
  • Series: King Cold - Nine Lives, Life II of IX

Turn it the other way and the predator is waiting - cut in brass and stainless steel, dropped flush into the copper. Around it, an ocean rendered in relief: sculpted wave-forms sealed beneath a hand-poured, glass-hard resin that gives the water real depth and movement under light. The Kraken watches from the corner.

Every coin is machined from a single copper billet, finished with the signature EDC milled edge, and hand-assembled - metal, leather, and resin, three disciplines living on one 1.35" face. Copper is a living surface. It will darken, warm, and record every round you carry it through. That patina isn't a flaw. It's the receipt.

Thirty pieces. Numbered. Blacklist only. Once they're gone, the food chain closes.

products.title: BLACKLIST 032: THE TORCHBEARER
products.body_html:
She holds the torch. We hold the flame.

THE TORCHBEARER is carbon steel taken to heat and held there - blued, then bled into pink and gold where the fire decided to linger. No two finishes are the same because no two passes of the torch are the same. The face of Liberty sits inlaid in hand-applied copper patina, green as old harbor metal. Turn it over: the Kraken, struck in the same verdigris, watching from the back.

The prongs are ours. Tentacles, not tines.

This is not a tool that asks permission. It marks. It repairs. It tells everyone within reach exactly who you are before you've said a word.

THE SPECIFICATIONS

  • Carbon steel, hand-torched
  • Hand-applied copper patina inlays - Liberty face (front), Kraken seal (back)
  • Kraken tentacle prongs
  • 2.8" L × 0.84" W × 0.25" thick
    37g
  • Ships with The Promenade - your numbered certificate of authenticity

THE NATURE OF THE PIECE
Every TORCHBEARER is one of one. The torch colors are placed by hand. The copper patina is living finish - it will deepen, darken, and shift the longer you carry it. The piece you receive is the youngest it will ever be.

THE TORCHBEARER - Thirty exist. Blacklist only. When they're gone, they're retired to The Vault.

CARE - CARBON STEEL
Carbon steel is alive. Treat it like it.

Keep it dry. Wipe it down after every round and after any contact with water, sweat, or grass.
A drop of light machine oil or mineral oil on a cloth, worked over the steel monthly, preserves the torch finish and holds back unwanted rust.
The copper patina is meant to evolve - leave it be. It will only get richer.
Do not polish, buff, or use abrasives. You'll strip the fire off it.
Store it in the capsule it came in.

Carry it. Mark with it. Let it age with you.

No two are alike. The color comes from the flame, not a swatch — some run gold and pink, others bruise to blue and purple. Thirty pieces, thirty different fires. Whatever lands in your hand is the only one of its kind. On the reverse, an homage to the open in deep relief - the kind of heft that turns a ball marker into something you carry whether you're playing that day or not.

products.title: 🏆 THE WATCHER - SOUTHAMPTON 2026 - LIMITED TO 50
products.body_html:
🏆 THE WATCHER - SOUTHAMPTON 2026 - LIMITED TO 50

This isn't just a marker. It's a vantage point.

The Captain came back. Not to lead the fight this time - to watch it. Anodized blue aluminum, deep as Atlantic water, with the Captain rising off the face: a stainless steel torso inked top to bottom - anchor, star, waves - the marks of a man who's logged more sea than most have logged fairways. A brass cap. Brass shades. Behind him, an acrylic ocean swell breaks in blue - the same water that guards the links where the championship comes ashore this June.

He's not clapping. He's not standing in the gallery rope line. He throws the horns and watches the establishment crown another one. Southampton, by the sea, where the wind decides who's worthy. The Captain already knew.

Flip it. A single Kraken mark, centered and quiet. The ocean-wave pattern runs edge to edge in white - the tide that never stops, the only tradition worth keeping.

The edge? My EDC standard. Tactile. Addictive. Every flip sounds like a wave hitting the rocks.

This is not a souvenir. It's a relic of the week the sea hosted the game. And with only 50 made, most golfers will only ever see one - from across the green.

Arachne was built as a predator's instrument - a piece defined by tension, patience, and the moment before impact. Every line, every weld bead, every polished surface was designed to feel alive. Not decorative. Not safe. Alive.

Built entirely from 303 stainless steel and weighing in at 375 grams, Arachne carries the kind of presence you feel before you ever make a stroke. That attachment method appears throughout the putter and matters to the piece. The beads are not hidden. They are part of the language of the build - raw, deliberate, and charged with energy. They give Arachne a live quality, as if the putter is still carrying the heat of its making.

In the back cavity, a larger polished web is welded in as well, joined by a small stainless steel spider fixed to the structure like it belongs there by instinct, not by decoration.

On the sole, the message is simple:

WAIT. READ. STRIKE.

Finished with the Kraken logo, it says exactly what this putter is about.

Each Arachne comes with a leather grip, headcover, and a certificate of authenticity. Only 5 pieces will be made. Each one is individually crafted and individually finished, which means slight differences in finish and character are part of the truth of the object, not a flaw. No two should feel factory identical, because they are not.

Arachne is not a mass-produced putter with a theme. Each of the 5 putters is one-of-one - spider position, weld points, torching and cavity inlays vary across every build.

It is a hand-finished weapon for the player who understands that the read comes first, the strike comes last, and patience is part of the kill.

products.title: Movember Skull Ball Marker
products.body_html:
Men’s health is in crisis. Men are dying on average 6 years earlier than women, and for largely preventable reasons.

Unchecked, prostate cancer rates will double over the next 15 years. Globally, testicular cancer is the most common cancer among men aged 15-39 years of age. And across the world, one man dies by suicide every minute of every day, with males accounting for 75% of all suicides.

Movember funds groundbreaking projects all over the world, engaging men where they are to understand what works best and accelerate change.

I am very much a supporter of this charity. To help in a small way, I will donate part of the proceeds from this release to the Movember charity. There will only be 30 units total available! 

The the Torched Skull Marker is my gamer! Only 30 units of these markers were produced for the release. This marker features an engraved skull with slick hair, mustache and pipe! products.title: 🍉 Slice Free Crayon Golf Divot Tool (Melon)
products.body_html:
This isn't a divot tool. It's a turf assassin in disguise.

Slice Free is a no-apologies, crayon-shaped weapon for green repair-machined from lightweight aircraft-grade aluminum, anodized in scorching Hot Pink, and wrapped in bold Lime Green waterproof vinyl that looks crayon-perfect and stays that way when conditions get ugly.

The 1" precision-milled tip drives into the turf smooth, lifts the scar back to life, and leaves the green cleaner than you found it. The CNC-cut curves keep the balance right in your hand-easy to carry, fast to deploy, and impossible to mistake for "normal golf gear."

It's not just a tool. It's a signal: you don't play the course's dress code. You play your game.

Story behind

Golf's full of quiet, safe gear that looks like it was designed by committee. Slice Free was built as the opposite-something that repairs greens properly while telegraphing attitude. The hot pink + lime combo is intentional: it's not trying to blend in. It's for the golfer who wants to be remembered before they hit their first shot.

Specs & features

  • Material: Lightweight aircraft-grade aluminum - durable, pocket-friendly, built to last
  • Finish: Hot Pink anodized body with glass bead-blasted grip texture
  • Wrap: Lime Green waterproof vinyl - crayon-perfect attitude, holds up to real use
  • Tip: CNC-milled 1" precision fork - smooth entry, clean repairs
  • Length: 3.5" Diameter: 0.375"
  • Weight: ~14g

Care note

Like all gear worth carrying, Slice Free will wear in over time. That patina isn't damage-it's proof you actually play.

products.title: Red Birdie Crayon Pitch Tool
